p: A few tips go a long way at a place like this. Donkeys are gentle, but they're also thoughtful animals that like to take their time, so encourage the kids to approach calmly, speak softly and let the donkey come to them. Flat hands and slow movements are the way to go, and the volunteers are the best people to ask about which animals enjoy a bit of fuss and which prefer to be admired from a step back.

Dress for a farmyard rather than a shopping trip. Wellies or old trainers are a sensible shout, and a spare pair of socks in the car never hurts if it's been wet. Because it's a sanctuary, the donkeys' welfare comes first, so don't bring your own treats unless staff say it's fine. A little patience usually earns you a nuzzle anyway.

Mill Rythe Lane is on the eastern side of the island, the quieter side that looks out towards Chichester Harbour, with its creeks, wading birds and big skies. It's a lovely contrast to the busier southern seafront. After your session, the Hayling Billy Trail is ideal for a flat walk or cycle along the old railway line, and the beaches along the south coast of the island are only a short drive away for a paddle, a picnic or an ice cream.
It's also a lovely way to show children that caring for animals is a full-time job, and that every donation makes a real difference to the donkeys who call this place home.
